- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or mean.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8) — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to account for mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day from day 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows strong negative sentiment (e.g., 0.1–0.3) followed by a rebound, model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% in first 3 days of rebound.
